Run a local database OAuth demo

Source: R/demo.R
oauth_db_demo.Rd

Try a Shiny app where visitors sign in and query a database with their own permissions. The package supplies a local database, Keycloak sign-in, demo accounts and sample data through Docker. You can run the app in Docker or local R without a cloud account or source checkout.

Usage

oauth_db_demo(
  database = c("postgres", "postgrest", "trino", "starrocks", "duckdb", "libsql",
    "cratedb", "opensearch"),
  action = c("start", "stop", "files", "services"),
  path = NULL,
  launch_browser = interactive(),
  build = TRUE,
  app = c("docker", "local")
)

Arguments

database

Demo to run: "postgres" (the default), "postgrest", "trino", "starrocks", "duckdb" (Quack), "libsql", "cratedb", or "opensearch".

action

"start" runs the demo until you stop it or interrupt R. "stop" removes its containers and data, including after a forced exit. "files" copies the configuration without starting Docker. "services" starts only the Docker services and returns settings for an app you run in the current R session; app is ignored in this mode.

path

Directory for the demo files. Defaults to a database-specific directory in R's user cache. Existing demo files are kept so you can edit the app or configuration. An unrelated nonempty directory is refused.

launch_browser

Open the app in your browser once it is ready. Services-only mode leaves browser launch to your app.

build

Build Docker images before starting. Set to FALSE to reuse images from a previous successful build.

app

Where to run the Shiny app: "docker" (the default) supplies its R environment and drivers, or "local" uses your installed R packages. Local mode creates an editable app under local-app/<database>/ in path.

Value

Invisibly, the directory containing the demo configuration. With action = "services", an environment containing provider (a configured shinyOAuth provider), url (the local data endpoint), host, port, ca_bundle (for HTTPS endpoints), path and a stop() function instead.

Details

Install and start Docker with Linux containers and Compose v2, then run oauth_db_demo(). The first build needs internet access, several minutes and a few GB of disk space.

Open http://localhost:18100 in a regular browser. Sign in as alice with password alice, or bob with password bob. Your browser may ask you to accept Keycloak's local test certificate at https://localhost:18443.

Run one demo at a time because they share ports. Click Stop demo or interrupt R to remove the containers and sample data. Copied files and cached images stay for later runs. After a forced exit, use action = "stop" with the same database, app mode and path.

The accounts and passwords are public demo settings. For your own deployment, follow the source's setup guide.

Run and edit the app locally

Use app = "local" to run Shiny with your installed R packages while Docker runs the database and sign-in service. Install callr and bslib 0.9.0 or later, plus the source's R client and database driver. PostgREST works without a database driver and is a useful first option.

Trino needs RTrino. StarRocks needs odbc and MySQL Connector/ODBC with its OpenID Connect plugin. DuckDB needs a matching client (1.5.4 for the demo) and its Quack extensions. Native PostgreSQL needs Linux with RPostgres and shinyOAuthDB linked to the same libpq 18.

Use action = "files" to copy the app, then edit local-app/<database>/app.R. Start with the same path, save your edits and reload the browser. Existing files are preserved; use a new empty path for fresh templates.

Local mode needs Compose 2.24.4 or later. It trusts the demo certificate only in the app process, leaving your certificate store unchanged. StarRocks needs about 4 GB of Docker memory and amd64 support; OpenSearch needs about 2 GB for its database container.

Run your own app with Docker services

Use action = "services" to start the database and sign-in service, then return to R without starting Shiny. This needs Compose 2.24.4 or later. Pass the returned provider to shinyOAuth::oauth_client() and url to the data helper. The PostgREST example works without a database driver; native clients still need their usual drivers.

Keep the returned handle, such as demo, while your app runs. Register demo$stop with shiny::onStop() or call demo$stop() when finished. It removes containers and sample data and restores local-development options. Reuse the handle until you stop it.

Browser sign-in uses HTTPS. Services-only PostgREST uses HTTP on 127.0.0.1:19444, allowed only while the demo is active. Other endpoints use HTTPS; the handle's ca_bundle supplies their local certificate.

See also

oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(), oauth_db_trino(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
oauth_db_demo()
oauth_db_demo("postgrest")
oauth_db_demo("trino")
oauth_db_demo("starrocks")
oauth_db_demo("duckdb")
oauth_db_demo("libsql")
oauth_db_demo("cratedb")
oauth_db_demo("opensearch")
oauth_db_demo(action = "stop")
path <- oauth_db_demo(action = "files")
# Edit a local R app backed by PostgreSQL and PostgREST in Docker:
path <- oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", action = "files")
file.edit(file.path(path, "local-app", "postgrest", "app.R"))
oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", path = path)
# Run your own app against PostgreSQL through PostgREST:
demo <- oauth_db_demo("postgrest", action = "services")
demo$provider
demo$url
demo$stop()
} # }
